comments.note: If useNativeSorting() or useManualSorting() is called after useCallbackSorting(), $sortCallback remains set while sortMode changes. getSortCallback() returns non-null even though mode is no longer Callback. This is benign since callers must check getSortMode() first (documented by Developer), but could cause confusion. Not a blocker — no AC requires cleanup of the callback on mode change.

No unit tests exist for the new sort API (SortMode enum, isSortable(), getSortMode(), getSortCallback()). The WP did not require new tests, and the implementation passes static analysis, but a dedicated ColumnSortTest class would improve confidence for WP-002 regression coverage.

summary: Code review PASS. SortMode enum, BaseGridColumn sort API, and GridColumnInterface updates are clean, minimal, and fully aligned with project conventions. All three files include declare(strict_types=1). The fluent API contract (return self) is consistently maintained. Closure::fromCallable() is the correct pattern for type-safe callable storage. No security, performance, or maintainability blocking issues found. Two non-blocking suggestions recorded in comments.

comments.note: BaseGridColumn::useNativeSorting() and useManualSorting() do not clear $sortCallback when the mode changes away from Callback. If a consumer calls ->useCallbackSorting(fn()=>0)->useNativeSorting(), getSortCallback() still returns a non-null Closure despite the mode being Native. Since callers are expected to guard with getSortMode() first this is technically safe, but it violates the principle of least astonishment and will become a subtle footgun when WP-002 consumers start querying the sort API. Recommendation: add $this->sortCallback = null inside useNativeSorting() and useManualSorting().

GridColumnInterface::getSortCallback() has no docblock. A one-line note documenting that this returns non-null only when getSortMode() === SortMode::Callback would help consumers avoid misuse without needing to inspect BaseGridColumn.

No dedicated unit test class exists for the sorting API (SortMode enum, isSortable(), getSortMode(), getSortCallback()). A ColumnSortTest class would provide regression coverage before WP-002 builds on top of this foundation. Not required now, but recommended before the feature is considered production-ready.
